claims.text: The wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu coating at high temperature is governed by grain size and the resulting grain-boundary sliding mechanism.
Microscopic deformation of the FeNiCrCoCu coating during high-temperature sliding is governed by grain size and the resulting grain-boundary sliding mechanism.
The baseline FeNiCrCoCu coating has an average grain size of 10 μm.
Annealing at 900°C for 1 hour can reduce the coating's average grain size from 10 μm to 1 μm.
The proposed comparison uses a sliding temperature of 500°C, a normal load of 10 N, and a sliding speed of 0.1 m/s.
Grain boundaries are the structural mediator connecting grain size to sliding response.
Grain-boundary sliding contributes to deformation and wear in the proposed operating regime.
Dislocation glide contributes to deformation and wear in the proposed operating regime.
Reducing average grain size from 10 μm to 1 μm will decrease wear rate by 30% relative to the baseline.
Reducing average grain size from 10 μm to 1 μm will decrease microscopic deformation by 25% relative to the baseline.
The predictions are intended to hold for grain sizes from 1 to 10 μm and temperatures from 400 to 600°C.
Coating thickness, substrate material, and testing conditions may also influence wear resistance and microscopic deformation.
The hypothesis is falsified if reducing grain size to 1 μm does not decrease both wear rate and microscopic deformation by at least 20%.
